source.stem:
A ray of light is reflected by a plane mirror.
Which row shows the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection?
angle of angle of incidence reflection

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: plane mirror is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: For a concave mirror, an object close to the mirror gives an erect, enlarged image.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when For a concave mirror, an object close to the mirror gives an erect, enlarged image is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: A plane mirror forms an erect image of the same size as the object; a concave mirror can change image size and orientation with object distance; a convex mirror forms an erect, smaller image. mirror type and object distance determine image size and orientation The learner identifies plane, concave, and convex mirrors from the size and orientation of the image they form. Any curved mirror can make any image size or orientation, so the image clues are not useful for naming the mirror.
